observation_summary: The method findWrapPos in HelpFormatter throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException because it attempts to access a character at an index equal to the string length, which is out of bounds. The bug report confirms this is due to an incorrect boundary check in a while loop.
hypothesis: The while loop condition 'pos <= text.length()' in findWrapPos is incorrect and should be 'pos < text.length()' to prevent accessing an index equal to the string length.
prediction: Changing the loop condition to 'pos < text.length()' will resolve the StringIndexOutOfBoundsException.
experiment_rationale: The bug report explicitly identifies the line and the fix (changing <= to <). The stack trace confirms the exception occurs at the exact line identified in the report.
reasoning_summary: The code snippet shows 'pos <= text.length()' in the while loop condition at line 937. Since 'text.charAt(pos)' is called inside the loop, if 'pos' equals 'text.length()', an exception is thrown. This is a classic boundary check error.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is a simple boundary check correction, not a change to the underlying algorithm or logic flow.
